searchText: Hey folks, a stupid question: what is the difference between `eth_call(<....>, 'latest')` and `eth_call(<.....>, 'pending')`? It looks to me that both latest and pending are the same in context of `eth_call` or are there some subtle differences? assume that I'm not a miner <@!520564582196969472> In *theory* `pending` means "construct what you think the next block is, and call this transaction against the state after that block". I'm not sure if all clients actually implement it like that though. <tkstanczak> pending is a special block that Geth constructs which is a prediction of the next block based on the tx pool observation <tkstanczak> Nethermind returns latest in both cases geth does construct it even in case when the mining is off? <tkstanczak> yes okay, so theoretically getting token balance using `eth_call` with `pending` at the same time could return different results in Nethermind and Geth just based on the tx pool? thanks for the info, it was a bit unclear from any of the docs I've seen Results may differ just from two different instances of the same client, who have different views of the current mempool. okay, gotcha thanks! <tkstanczak> it was a mystery for us for over a year too
